title: Incident command, postmortem & mitigation roadmap for dedicated capacity shortfall
creator: Marco Hernandez
description: Summary: On 2026-02-19 we observed a sustained capacity shortfall affecting multiple Dedicated pools that resulted in elevated latency and several SLA warnings for enterprise customers. The immediate incident response stabilized customer traffic but revealed configuration drift and observability gaps in autoscaling and pool orchestration. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations taken, and a prioritized mitigation roadmap (short/medium/long-term).
incident_timeline: 2026-02-19 01:45 UTC: First automated SLO alert (p95 latency) triggered for dedicated-pool-us-west-1
2026-02-19 01:52 UTC: Incident commander (Sofia) paged; on-call runbook initiated
2026-02-19 02:05 UTC: Observed repeated scale-up failures for warm nodes due to failed kernel-selection job (OOM in kernel-selector service)
2026-02-19 02:22 UTC: Temporary diversion policy applied: route low-priority workloads to burst-capacity tenant and enable degradation rules
2026-02-19 03:10 UTC: Manual pool rebalancing executed to move reserved capacity between tenant groups; customer impact reduced
2026-02-19 05:40 UTC: Autoscaler config rolled back to last-known-good; scaling resumed for affected pools
2026-02-19 07:00 UTC: All affected SLO alerts returned to normal; incident declared mitigated but not fully resolved
2026-02-20 10:00 UTC: Post-incident triage and timeline reconstruction started
root_cause: A combination of a recent autoscaler config change (dynamic warm-pool sizing) and an untested kernel-selection refactor caused sporadic OOMs in the kernel-selector service. Those OOMs prevented hot-path scale-up decisions from completing under load. The autoscaler lacked a fast-fail fallback path and depended on the kernel-selector for capacity gating, which led to delayed or dropped scale-ups and transient capacity shortfalls.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back autoscaler warm-pool sizing configuration to previous stable values (2026-02-19 03:10 UTC)
Enabled emergency diversion policy to route low-priority workloads to configurable burst-capacity (applied 02:22 UTC)
Increased alert thresholds for kernel-selector OOMs and opened emergency patch PR to add faster health checks
Manually rebalanced reserved capacity between affected tenant groups to reduce immediate customer impact
affected_customers_summary: ~4 enterprise customers experienced increased p95 latency and one customer reported degraded throughput for 2.5 hours. No data loss or confidentiality issues reported.
postmortem_summary: Configuration drift combined with a regression in kernel-selection path produced scale-up failures under load. Immediate mitigations restored service stability; longer-term fixes are required for autoscaler resiliency, detection, and safer rollout of kernel-selector changes.
decisions: Block merging any kernel-selector refactor to main until a regression test harness and canary pipeline are in place
Introduce fast-fail path in autoscaler: if kernel-selector is unhealthy, autoscaler will use conservative heuristics to scale rather than blocking
Create a small 'reserved surge' pool for enterprise customers to protect SLOs during short regressions
Add automated chaos tests for autoscaler and kernel-selection interactions in CI
short_term_actions: (Sofia) Harden observability: add dedicated kernel-selector OOM metric and dashboard (due 2026-02-27)
(Alex) Implement autoscaler fast-fail fallback and emergency toggle (due 2026-03-05)
(Priya) Create runbook patch to prefer conservative scale heuristics when kernel-selector latency > 2s (due 2026-02-28)
(Infra) Reserve 'surge' capacity of 3 nodes per enterprise pool to absorb short regressions (pilot, due 2026-03-10)
medium_term_actions: Build a canary pipeline for kernel-selector refactors with workload replay (owner: Eng Reliability, due 2026-04-01)
Enhance autoscaler regression detection: add rate-of-failure and state machine checkpoints (owner: Autoscale team, due 2026-04-15)
Implement warm-pool simulation tests to validate new sizing algorithms under realistic load (owner: Serving Runtime, due 2026-04-30)
long_term_actions: Introduce a capacity reservation API so customers can optionally purchase 'guardrails' for critical routes (product + eng, roadmap 2026-Q3)
Refactor kernel-selector into a sidecar pattern to reduce blast radius of memory pressure (owner: Runtime, research in 2026-Q3)
Continuous quality: schedule quarterly chaos experiments targeting dedicated autoscaling and pool orchestration
action_items: ENG-11003: Add kernel-selector OOM and latency panels to Grafana and Datadog (owner: Alex, due 2026-02-27)
ENG-11004: Implement autoscaler fallback toggle and test harness (owner: Priya, due 2026-03-05)
ENG-11005: Pilot reserved surge pools for top 10 enterprise customers (owner: Theo, due 2026-03-10)
PM-412: Update SLA docs and customer comms template for capacity incidents (owner: Rachel, due 2026-03-12)
follow_up_meetings: 2026-03-17 10:00 UTC: Pilot reserved surge pool retrospective
notes: Trade-off: reserving surge capacity increases cost baseline; we recommend pilot with top customers before committing to broad reservation
Partial decision: will prefer autoscaler fast-fail + conservative heuristics over optimistic blocking behavior to prioritize availability
Monitoring gap identified: kernel-selector internal retries were not surfaced to higher-level metrics; added to short-term observability work
approvals_and_feedback: PM review (Rachel): supports reserved surge pilot for high-SLA customers
Security review: no immediate concerns; will re-evaluate sidecar plan during design phase
Design review: dashboard mockups approved (see ENG-11003)
